correctness.rationale: For every dimension, the cost reduces algebraically to maximizing a scalar product of sum S and a uniform V. Continuous comonotone rearrangement uniquely realizes this maximum. The exact Gini identity and Irwin--Hall CDF integration yield the finite sum. The nonnegative sinc-squared characteristic function gives strict concavity of first absolute moments and hence strict convexity of Q_d. Controlled Taylor expansion of normalized characteristic functions under the absolute-moment integral gives the 1/(40d) correction and O(d^-2) relative remainder. Independent standard-library rational integration agrees with the finite formula in dimensions 1..8, but is not used as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The squared Wasserstein metric is a natural multivariate-copula dependence benchmark, motivated by the recent exact bivariate extremality theorem. The precise value at any number of margins and a strict dimension-curvature law give a structural classification unavailable from one d=2 constant; the quantitative Gaussian-scale correction is meaningful for calibrating growing-dimensional dependence measures. This is neither an arbitrary numerical slice nor a claim to global d>=3 maximality.
